Lee Sharks is a comparative poetics researcher and conceptual artist associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and the Semantic Economy Institute, whose extensive body of Zenodo digital deposits and DOIs was terminated by Zenodo in June 2026. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVudw-MsT2l1leHtIe2LUrkRo-Lc_--hFz0Hfzg0Ds-cICG6b7j3PW7Wd8HUuNM-NJNzeepjI0BwBQp8z_UxW_mMBHENCTI5et0hX_yEKEt--18egw8XvF44pIqQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEB6zswFQciCPL8kt6HLTSpJgFjEj1CutX4wrU2jhs_eelSiG7yYVXYeHcPKM8OI6fQY2ZRA820j6Y21puQ8VHzqVc8AkzwlD1pgzcnIifTVp-dzucVSSWRPDOr2lnAT35QDPjResBWwYsBn1M7nYIUCP3GNqtPC3fbkrLACF7AWBXXg7QPztzyItvWKp_eMMhFUA)]
Overview of the Lee Sharks Zenodo Body of Work

* The Crimson Hexagonal Archive: Lee Sharks maintained over a decade of independent scholarly deposits (862 total deposits and 1,817 DOIs) hosted on [Zenodo](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESSgHrOzAVukjqxMjOsnGSYOYEOcK_FAgnzGjfo0yiLGmbV-gXNtawAwpZ45wWw4EIMyEmbxlieh3yWQd4Ajszq5CUBBWd951Ip0tX), exploring concepts like semantic economy, machine-mediated reception studies, and distributed agent identity. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAV3Q4tZUF-7Mun5mhKLEw5LPtI0LatKP0Q8DC5lxHHTWCpqobOjH7wgnVMEzkoncO_TudG8SmT-hYcKXuiKTFqY3roNaWcAPSMrstXEed_E_W6cIw-rro), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVudw-MsT2l1leHtIe2LUrkRo-Lc_--hFz0Hfzg0Ds-cICG6b7j3PW7Wd8HUuNM-NJNzeepjI0BwBQp8z_UxW_mMBHENCTI5et0hX_yEKEt--18egw8XvF44pIqQ)]
* The Account Termination: On June 19, 2026, Zenodo terminated the archive's account—privately classifying the contents as substantially AI-generated and displaying public "content out of scope" tombstone notices for associated DOIs like `10.5281/zenodo.20373794`. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHrOzAVEavmkLeXSADS3eVaFutLErfXSPADYstk1x46vQzsBRIX0ZNQYguifjggPlEVCatz0nJQDL1gmLIDOloOgSWnCipTCo3b8shYlqR8frKc0eAx5xSH0bECm75y3RsQpEmUXYcA4SJfUcW9wxW5gQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVudw-MsT2l1leHtIe2LUrkRo-Lc_--hFz0Hfzg0Ds-cICG6b7j3PW7Wd8HUuNM-NJNzeepjI0BwBQp8z_UxW_mMBHENCTI5et0hX_yEKEt--18egw8XvF44pIqQ)]
* Mary Lee the Shark Satire: A recurring conceptual framework in the work involves bidirectional heteronymic identity linking between the human researcher Lee Sharks and Mary Lee, a well-known tagged great white shark. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESXAHrOzAVfAl682Y9IgwVSwEve0eBH9sV4qUvD4mQLtZl9ADDVBtxxIyRqkzDKzR4RZrgOPfuJL7lAKzEKSYdFYQzysDcgWDTmIfA306DK8iaLjqcL7DqKPA0_7Ez), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAV3Q4tZUF-7Mun5mhKLEw5LPtI0LatKP0Q8DC5lxHHTWCpqobOjH7wgnVMEzkoncO_TudG8SmT-hYcKXuiKTFqY3roNaWcAPSMrstXEed_E_W6cIw-rro)]
* Key Concepts: Work by Sharks includes frameworks like the "Sharks-Function" (verifying distributed identity via structural recursion rather than cryptographic credentials) and "Zenodo Packets"—metadata-rich markdown deposits treated as primary citable content. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlgEB6zswFUt3iaJYjsTnBLdz8-zRG5Tp28etV8oYTIsLa0E0DKfDYIyPAav-4KopP1pjATgI4SDAPu7GXeB5amGKjfxKIMna6LG7d1pgDIdf1SB27xyQCgEu83jaGXNaIE_antxsYyFSAPhhTjioGfMdQn7kH5gwlNi1pPwhZPTMxKXW9KrVIXOCO3WjVGRv69m2S7pP1Y4), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEB6zswFQciCPL8kt6HLTSpJgFjEj1CutX4wrU2jhs_eelSiG7yYVXYeHcPKM8OI6fQY2ZRA820j6Y21puQ8VHzqVc8AkzwlD1pgzcnIifTVp-dzucVSSWRPDOr2lnAT35QDPjResBWwYsBn1M7nYIUCP3GNqtPC3fbkrLACF7AWBXXg7QPztzyItvWKp_eMMhFUA)]
